after.reason: Raffi’s personal isolation is not evidence of a distinct Federation material regime; retain as a contextual comparison linked to the existing core record.
after.analysis:
The saved source is a critic’s interpretation of Raffi as near-poor. It does not establish a changed entitlement, different productive ownership or a separate automation model. Emotional isolation and addiction are not themselves denial of food or shelter.

The best guess is continuity of the broad Federation material model, with this later personal case kept as a qualification rather than a second counted economy. This is an economic-model duplicate, not a claim that every era or person experiences identical conditions.
after.follow_up: No full-series reconstruction required. Reopen a separate society only if a distinct production/access rule is identified.

after.reason: Sargus 4 is a reputation-punishment comparison, not an established labor-substitution society; save explicit coordinates without counting it toward the post-work target.
after.analysis:
Sargus 4 automates and crowdsources social judgment through reputation votes. That establishes a coercive allocation of status and punishment, while the available episode reference supplies no productive labor replacement or material floor. Importing the Union’s synthesizers would describe a different society.

The comparison is nevertheless scored as requested: weak guarantees, concentrated effective social power despite mass voting, and ordinary ongoing participation are the central best guesses. These numbers are not a claim that reputation voting makes the society post-work. The definite mechanism being classified is social punishment, so this remains a completed outside-scope comparison rather than a lore-gap research hold.
after.follow_up: Comparison analyzed under the current policy; no deep reading needed. A future material-production mechanism could justify reassessment.
